title: Is It Love… or Just Physical Attraction Disguised?
paragraphs:
Is It Love… or Just Physical Attraction Disguised?
The difference could save your soul… or slowly destroy it.
You didn’t mean to fall this deep.

It started with a glance that lingered a second too long… a conversation that felt easy… a presence that made your heart race in ways you hadn’t felt in years. It felt alive. It felt real. It felt like love.
But somewhere, deep inside, there’s a quiet question you’ve been avoiding.
Is this love… or just desire wearing a mask?

Because the truth is, not everything that feels powerful is pure. Not everything that pulls you closer is sent to build you. Some things feel like heaven at first… but slowly pull you away from God, one compromise at a time.
Scripture doesn’t stay silent about this.

In the Greek, the New Testament uses different words for what we casually call “love.” There’s ἔρως (eros)—a passionate, physical desire. There’s φιλία (philia)—a brotherly, emotional bond. But the love that God commands… the love that transforms… is ἀγάπη (agapē).
And ἀγάπη is not driven by feelings. It is driven by sacrifice.

“Love is patient, love is kind…”
In the original Greek, 1 Corinthians 13:4 begins with ἡ ἀγάπη μακροθυμεῖ, χρηστεύεται ἡ ἀγάπη—a love that endures long and actively chooses kindness, even when it’s inconvenient.
Now be honest.

What you’re feeling right now… is it patient?
Is it holy?
Is it leading you closer to Christ… or quietly pulling you into compromise?
Because attraction can feel urgent. It wants now. It demands closeness before commitment. It whispers, “If it feels right, it must be right.”
But the Word of God confronts that lie directly.
In Hebrew, Proverbs 4:23 says, מִכָּל־מִשְׁמָר נְצֹר לִבֶּךָ—“Above all guarding, guard your heart.”
Why would God command you to guard your heart… if everything that feels good is safe?
Because some connections are not sent to bless you. Some are sent to test what you truly value.

There are relationships that feel intense but are rooted in σάρξ (sarx)—the flesh. Galatians 5:19 speaks of the works of the flesh, and they often begin subtly… through desire, through emotional dependency, through a bond that feels strong but is spiritually empty.
And here’s the part that hurts.
You can be deeply attached to someone… and still be outside of God’s will.
That tension you feel? That quiet conviction you keep ignoring? That moment after the conversation ends and something doesn’t sit right in your spirit?
That’s not anxiety.
That’s the Holy Spirit refusing to let you settle for something less than God’s best.
Because real love… God’s love… doesn’t confuse you, rush you, or pull you away from righteousness.
It leads you into light.
1 John 4:8 says, ὁ θεὸς ἀγάπη ἐστίν—“God is love.” Not desire. Not obsession. Not emotional dependency. God is agapē.
So if what you’re experiencing consistently pulls you away from Him… it may feel like love, but it’s not sourced from Him.
And this is where the Gospel interrupts your story.
Because maybe you’ve already crossed lines. Maybe you’ve already given parts of your heart, your body, your attention to something you now realize wasn’t love.
Maybe you feel ashamed. Confused. Stuck.
But listen carefully.
Jesus doesn’t step into your story to condemn you. He steps in to rewrite you.
The woman caught in sin expected stones. Instead, she heard grace.
In John 8:11, Jesus says, οὐδὲ ἐγώ σε κατακρίνω· πορεύου καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν μηκέτι ἁμάρτανε—“Neither do I condemn you; go, and from now on sin no more.”
That is not permission to continue.
That is power to begin again.
This is where love becomes real.
Not in the intensity of how someone looks at you… but in the transformation of how Christ changes you.
Because true love doesn’t just make your heart race.
It makes your soul clean again.
So ask yourself, without filters, without excuses…
Is this drawing me closer to Jesus… or slowly pulling me away?
Be honest.
This hit deeper than you expected, didn’t it?
You’re not alone in this.
There are people reading this right now battling the same confusion, the same pull, the same conviction. Your honesty might be the thing that frees someone else.
If you truly want to glorify God with your life, your relationships, your choices… then support what feeds your spirit.
You don’t need more confusion.
You need truth… and the courage to follow it.
Because one day you will look back and realize… it was never about how strong the feeling was, but how aligned it was with God.
And that realization will either heal you… or break you.
